name: dsu_empty
why: n=0 with no operations: no states are produced.

name: dsu_example
why: Statement example. 4 singletons; {0,1}; {0,1,2}; repeated union changes nothing; self-union changes nothing.

name: dsu_merge_two_groups
why: Start 5 comps. [0,1]->4,2; [2,3]->3,2; [1,0] repeat; [4,4] self; [1,3] merges two pairs->2,4; [3,4] joins last vertex->1,5.

name: dsu_no_ops_single
why: One vertex, no operations: states stay empty (no initial state is printed).

name: kruskal_example
why: Statement example. Cheapest edges 1 (w2) and 2 (w3) span {0,1,2}; edge 0 would close a cycle; vertex 3 isolated -> cost 5, 2 components.

name: prim_example
why: Same graph as kruskal_example solved by Prim; optimum cost and component count must agree.

name: kruskal_loops_parallel_negative
why: Loop with weight -5 must NOT be taken. Parallel 0-1: take -2 not 3. Two equal 1-2 edges of weight 7: take one. Components {0,1,2},{3},{4}: cost -2+7=5, 3 components, 2 edges.

name: prim_loops_parallel_negative
why: Same graph as above for Prim (restarts for isolated vertices 3 and 4).

name: kruskal_total_beyond_32bit
why: All weights 1e9; any spanning tree has 3 edges: 3,000,000,000 > 2^31-1. Tests 64-bit sums.

name: prim_total_beyond_32bit
why: Same graph for Prim.

name: kruskal_empty
why: n=0: cost 0, no edges, 0 components.

name: prim_empty
why: n=0 for Prim.

name: scc_example
why: Statement example. 0<->1 form one SCC; 2 and 3 are singletons. Cross pairs: {0,1}->{2} (twice, deduplicated), {2}->{3}. Reps (min vertex): [0,2],[2,3].

name: scc_duplicates_loop_isolate
why: Cycle 0->1->2->0 is one SCC. Edges 2->3 (twice) and 1->3 give ONE pair {0,1,2}->{3}. Loop 3->3 is internal. 4->3 gives pair {4}->{3}. Vertex 5 isolated.

name: scc_empty
why: n=0: both arrays empty.

name: scc_two_cycles
why: SCCs {0,1} and {2,3,4}; only cross edge 1->2 -> single pair [0,2].

name: topo_example
why: Statement example: 0 and 1 before 2, 2 before 3. Acyclic.

name: topo_cycle
why: Cycle 0->1->2->0 (vertex 3 hangs off it): not acyclic, order must be empty.

name: topo_self_loop
why: A self-loop is a cycle.

name: topo_diamond_duplicates
why: Diamond with a duplicate edge. Edge to an already FINISHED vertex (2->3 after 1->3) is not a cycle, so acyclic=true.

name: topo_empty
why: n=0: acyclic with empty order.

name: dag_example
why: Statement example. 0->1 (3), 1->2 (-7) gives dist[2]=-4 (better than 8), 2->3 (4) gives 0; vertex 4 unreachable -> null.

name: dag_cycle_unreachable_from_source
why: Cycle 2<->3 is NOT reachable from source 0, but the whole graph must be checked: acyclic=false and empty arrays.

name: dag_parallel_and_tied
why: Parallel edges 0->1 (ids 0,1, w5). Vertex 2 reachable by id3 (5) or by 0->1->2 (5+0): tie. Distances [0,5,5]; either parent is valid.

name: dag_minus_one_is_finite
why: Distance -1 for vertex 1 is a real value; vertex 2 is unreachable and must be null (not -1).

name: dag_source_in_middle
why: Source 2: vertices 0 and 1 (before the source in the chain) are unreachable; relaxation never starts from them.

name: dag_single_vertex
why: n=1: only the source, distance [0].

name: dag_self_loop
why: A self-loop makes the graph cyclic.
